\section[la manifestación]{la manifestación — the demonstration, the protest march}

\label{lesson:ES-C570-manifestacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to defend, then the Spanish for the conflict.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la manifestación}
\textbf{la manifestación} — \textquotedblleft{}the demonstration, the protest march\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Miles de personas fueron a la manifestación.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Thousands of people went to the demonstration.}
\end{quote}

In Spain people often say \emph{la mani}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{manifestación} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{manifestātiō} 'a showing' (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{manifestus} 'plain to see'. A demonstration shows what people want.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la manifestación}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la manifestación}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la manifestación}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to defend, then the Spanish for the conflict, then say \emph{la manifestación} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la manifestación mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The demonstration, the protest march\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la protesta]{la protesta — the protest}

\label{lesson:ES-C570-protesta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the conflict, then the Spanish for the demonstration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la protesta}
\textbf{la protesta} — \textquotedblleft{}the protest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hubo protestas en todo el país.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There were protests all over the country.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{protesta} is built on \emph{protestar}, from Latin \emph{prōtestārī} 'to declare in public, to bear witness' (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{testis} 'a witness'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la protesta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la protesta}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the conflict, then the Spanish for the demonstration, then say \emph{la protesta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la protesta mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The protest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[el disturbio]{el disturbio — the disturbance, the riot}

\label{lesson:ES-C570-disturbio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the demonstration, then the Spanish for the protest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el disturbio}
\textbf{el disturbio} — \textquotedblleft{}the disturbance, the riot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hubo disturbios en el centro después del partido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There was rioting in the centre after the match.}
\end{quote}

Usually in the plural: \emph{los disturbios}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{disturbio} is built on \emph{disturbar} (EtymDB), a learned word from Latin \emph{disturbāre} 'to throw into disorder' (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{turba} 'an uproar, a crowd'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el disturbio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el disturbio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the demonstration, then the Spanish for the protest, then say \emph{el disturbio} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[el escándalo]{el escándalo — the scandal; the racket}

\label{lesson:ES-C570-escandalo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the protest, then the Spanish for the disturbance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el escándalo}
\textbf{el escándalo} — \textquotedblleft{}the scandal; the racket\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El escándalo salió en todos los periódicos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The scandal was in all the newspapers.}
\end{quote}

It also means a lot of noise: \emph{¡Qué escándalo!}

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{escándalo} is a learned borrowing from Church Latin \emph{scandalum}, taken from Greek \emph{skándalon} 'a stumbling block' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the protest, then the Spanish for the disturbance, then say \emph{el escándalo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la polémica]{la polémica — the controversy}

\label{lesson:ES-C570-polemica}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the disturbance, then the Spanish for the scandal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la polémica}
\textbf{la polémica} — \textquotedblleft{}the controversy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La nueva ley creó mucha polémica.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The new law caused a lot of controversy.}
\end{quote}

As an adjective: \emph{una ley polémica} — a controversial law.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{polémica} comes from Greek \emph{polemikós} 'warlike' (EtymDB), built on \emph{pólemos} 'war'. A controversy is a war of words.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la polémica}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la polémica}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la polémica}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the disturbance, then the Spanish for the scandal, then say \emph{la polémica} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la polémica mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The controversy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
